assignment_html:
Scenario

Purpose: Write a reusable Bug2 route calculation instead of solving only one displayed map.

A robot starts at O = (0, 0) and travels east toward G = (10, 0) along the Bug2 m-line. The displayed obstacle uses H = (4, 0), A = (4, -1), B = (6, -1), and L = (6, 0).

The required right-turn route is O -> H -> A -> B -> L -> G.

Task

Complete calculate_bug_route(start, hit, corner_a, corner_b, leave, goal). It must return these four values in order:

  1. Euclidean distance from start to hit.
  2. Boundary distance hit-to-corner_a plus corner_a-to-corner_b plus corner_b-to-leave.
  3. Euclidean distance from leave to goal.
  4. The sum of those three traveled components exactly once.

distance = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2)

Rules

  • Follow exactly H -> A -> B -> L. Do not use C, D, the upper boundary, or the full perimeter.
  • Use the function parameters. The grader also checks other coordinate scenarios.
  • Do not change the function name, parameters, return order, or starter call.

Scope and scoring

You are calculating a supplied route, not implementing the Bug2 hit/leave decision or controlling a simulated robot. Each point is an (x, y) pair measured in the same distance units. The helper calculates the distance between two points; your route function combines the required segments.

  • Each of the four returned components is worth 25%. A component earns credit only when it is correct for every grading scenario, not just the displayed map.
  • Partial work can earn 25%, 50%, or 75%. Syntax errors, runtime errors, or an invalid return count must be fixed before calculations can be evaluated.
  • Return exactly four numeric values in the stated order. Do not round intermediate calculations or returned values. You may round only the printed display.
  • Run tests shows your score and feedback. AI tutoring is optional, off by default, and cannot change your grade.

Before you run the tests

  • Confirm that the boundary distance contains exactly three segments.
  • Confirm that the total contains the approach, boundary, and departure components once each.
learning_objectives: Locate Bug2 hit and leave points where a rectangular obstacle intersects the m-line.
Translate a specified right-turn boundary route into Euclidean line segments.
Distinguish the traveled boundary distance from the full obstacle perimeter.
Compose a complete path length without omitting or double-counting segments.
